data.one_liner: Console and logging text coloring and styling library using ANSI and HTML modes.
data.what_it_does: Provides an expressive, chainable API for coloring and styling text in the terminal or console using ANSI codes. It also supports switching to HTML output mode for sending styled logs to a server or browser.
use_when: You want colorful, styled logs in the console or terminal during debugging.
You need to output styled text that can be viewed both in ANSI terminals and as HTML in a browser.
avoid_when: You require zero-allocation styling libraries for performance-critical hot paths (where quectocolors is recommended instead).
You do not need text styling or logging enhancements.
strengths: Supports full ANSI and HTML output modes with seamless switching.
Allows deep nesting of colors and styles.
Includes optional string extensions for concise usage.
weaknesses: Adds overhead compared to ultra-lightweight zero-allocation alternatives.
Relies on terminal or IDE support for ANSI rendering (though companion extensions exist for XCode/VSCode).
data.setup_notes: No native dependencies or build_runner required; just add to pubspec.
